preface.title: Preface
preface.para: This book describes ooRexx/.NET, a native bridge between Open Object Rexx and .NET that works both ways. An ooRexx program uses .NET's classes (the framework's, an assembly of your own, a COM object on Windows) as Rexx objects; a .NET program, written in C#, VB.NET, F# or PowerShell, creates ooRexx interpreters, runs Rexx code, and uses Rexx objects as .NET objects.

This book is a reference rather than a tutorial. It assumes you know ooRexx, and enough of .NET to read the documentation of the .NET classes you want to use, at https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/. Its companion, ooRexx and .NET: Cookbook, introduces the main concepts through short programs that can be run as they are.

Sections that document a concept carry a small example: a complete program, followed by what it prints. Every one of them that does not need Windows is run, and its output checked, by the project's tests on Linux, macOS and Windows; the Windows ones are run on Windows.

section.title: Related Information
section.para: See also ooRexx and .NET: Cookbook, Open Object Rexx: Reference, and the .NET documentation at https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/. How the bridge is built, and why each choice was made, is in the design notes of the project's repository, notes/netobject-design.md (ooRexx using .NET) and notes/rexx-from-net-design.md (.NET using ooRexx).
